question:
B. Is this measure already running in South Savo wellbeing services county (or in the KYS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Video MDT review of every stage I-III patient with the university hospital. Every patient whose cancer has not spread (stage I-III) is discussed by video with the university hospital lung team (surgeon, radiotherapy doctor, oncologist) before anyone decides against treatment that aims to cure. Today a county hospital can decide alone.
effect_summary_en: One UK district hospital (62 patients, before-after, 2004) saw its annual resection rate rise by 30% (relative) after video MDT meetings began; this is a small, old study and does not measure a share of all patients.
supported_en: A UK study (J Telemed Telecare 2004) reports the annual resection rate rose by 30% after telemedicine MDTs started.
not_supported_en: The pages do not show the assumed gain of 1.5 percentage points in the curative share in a Finnish setting.
in_use_quote: Moniammatillinen meeting kokoontuu viikoittain. Paikalla ovat thorax-kirurgi, patologi, radiologi, onkologi ja keuhkolääkäreitä. Jokaisen keuhkosyöpäpotilaan tilanne käsitellään ainakin kertaalleen kokouksessa, jossa tehdään hoitopäätös.
missing_en: No page shows that Mikkeli or Savonlinna join the KYS lung cancer MDT by video, or that every stage I-III patient from South Savo is discussed there.
summary_en: I found only part of this measure running. KYS Syövänhoitokeskus's lung cancer care pathway (2021) says a weekly meeting with a chest surgeon, pathologist, radiologist, oncologist and lung doctors discusses every lung cancer patient at least once to decide treatment. That pathway is a KYS document and does not say it covers South Savo's own hospitals. FICAN says Mikkeli already joins KYS's upper-GI and lower-GI cancer meetings by video, but it says nothing about a lung meeting. On effect, the only study I read is a small UK one from 2004: a district hospital's annual surgery rate rose by 30% after video meetings started. That points the right way but is weaker evidence than the size we assume.
unanswered_en: I found no page saying that Mikkeli or Savonlinna join the KYS lung cancer meeting by video, or that every stage I-III patient from South Savo is discussed there.
